regulations.title: Permit to Operate a food premises (Food Premises Regulation)
regulations.summary: Any business that manufactures, prepares, packages, or stores food for sale to the public in BC needs a Permit to Operate from its regional health authority before opening. This covers commercial kitchens, bakeries, and packaged-food production facilities.
regulations.regulation_name: Food Premises Regulation (B.C. Reg. 210/99), under the Public Health Act
regulations.authority: Regional health authorities (e.g., Fraser Health, Vancouver Coastal Health, Interior Health) under the BC Public Health Act
regulations.action_required: Submit a Permit to Operate application to the regional health authority covering your production location and food category, and complete the required facility review before selling any product.
regulations.penalty_note: Operating a food premises without a valid permit is an offence under the Public Health Act; a health authority can order the premises closed until it is compliant, in addition to fines.

regulations.title: FOODSAFE Level 1 certification for food handlers
regulations.summary: Under the Food Premises Regulation, the operator of a food business and at least one staff member on-site must hold a FOODSAFE Level 1 certificate (or an approved equivalent) covering safe food handling and sanitation.
regulations.authority: BC Ministry of Health / regional health authorities (FOODSAFE program)
regulations.action_required: Enroll the operator and at least one employee in a FOODSAFE Level 1 (or recognized equivalent) course and keep the certificate on file at the premises; it is valid for 5 years.
regulations.penalty_note: A food premises without a certified food handler on staff can be refused a permit or flagged on inspection, which can delay opening or trigger a compliance order.
regulations.source_name: Province of British Columbia - Food Safety Courses

regulations.title: Pre-opening and ongoing health authority inspection
regulations.summary: Before your Permit to Operate is issued, an environmental health officer inspects your kitchen or production facility for sanitation and layout compliance, and can return for unannounced follow-up inspections once you are open.
regulations.regulation_name: Food Premises Regulation (B.C. Reg. 210/99) - inspection provisions
regulations.authority: Regional health authorities (e.g., Fraser Health, Vancouver Coastal Health, Interior Health)
regulations.action_required: Prepare your production facility to meet health authority sanitation standards (handwashing stations, food-contact surfaces, pest control, storage) and book the pre-opening inspection.
regulations.penalty_note: A failed inspection blocks permit issuance or renewal until deficiencies are corrected and re-inspected; repeat violations can lead to permit suspension.
regulations.source_name: Fraser Health - Requirements for new food businesses

regulations.title: PST registration for taxable packaged food items
regulations.summary: Most basic groceries are exempt from BC's Provincial Sales Tax, but items like candy, snack foods, and soft drinks are taxable. If any of your packaged food falls into a taxable category, you must register with the Ministry of Finance and collect 7% PST on those items.
regulations.action_required: Review which of your packaged food products are PST-taxable (snack foods, candy, soft drinks) and register for a PST number with eTaxBC before selling them in BC.
regulations.penalty_note: Selling taxable goods without registering can lead to retroactive PST assessment plus penalties and interest under the Provincial Sales Tax Act.
regulations.source_name: Province of British Columbia - PST exemptions

regulations.title: Packaging and Paper Product producer (Recycle BC) registration
regulations.summary: If you supply packaged food to BC households (directly, online, or through retailers) and aren't a small, single-location exemption, you're a "producer" under BC's Recycling Regulation and must register with Recycle BC to fund and report on recycling of your packaging.
regulations.regulation_name: Recycling Regulation (B.C. Reg. 449/2004), Schedule 5 - Packaging and Printed Paper
regulations.authority: Recycle BC, under the BC Ministry of Environment and Parks' Recycling Regulation
regulations.action_required: Confirm whether you qualify for the small-producer exemption (under $1M BC revenue, under 1 tonne of packaging supplied, or single non-chain retail location); if not, register as a steward with Recycle BC and report your packaging volumes.
regulations.penalty_note: Producers who don't join an approved plan can face enforcement under the Recycling Regulation and Environmental Management Act, including compliance orders and fines.
regulations.source_name: Recycle BC - Are You a Steward?
